verdict.rationale: Pipecat's production telephony docs describe inbound calls arriving from the user's own carrier (Twilio, Telnyx, Plivo, Exotel, or a SIP provider) via the user's webhook, so the bot is not locked to bundled telephony; the homepage lists SIP and PSTN transports, and the dev runner documents a Twilio mode. However, the evidence never documents SIP trunk or PBX configuration in depth, so only part of the story is shown. missing for 10: documented SIP trunking / PBX connection setup (registration, trunk configuration), explicit number-import or BYO-number workflow for Pipecat Cloud, independent or hands-on corroboration of carrier/SIP interoperability.

support.subject: As a platform-engineer, I can connect my own carrier or PBX via SIP trunking (or import Twilio/Telnyx numbers) instead of being locked to bundled telephony

citations.quote: the carrier (Twilio, Telnyx, Plivo, Exotel, or your SIP provider) is calling your webhook to tell you there's an inbound call
